titleEn: Feeling Angry? Breathe on the Window!

pages.text: "My seat! Move!" Bami stamped by the dining-car window. Pipi had come down from the cold roof to warm up near the stove. Bami wanted that seat to watch snowy mountains.
"Chirp. I'll just warm up, then go." Pipi fluffed their feathers. "Move now!" Bami pecked the table and shouted. Startled, Pipi fluttered onto a shelf.
The dining car fell quiet except for the crackling stove. Mom turned from packing lunches. Pipi hid their head in their feathers. The seat was free, but Bami wasn't happy. Tears gathered.
Mom sat beside Bami. "Something hot rushed into your chest?" Bami sniffled and nodded. "That's a visitor called anger. It comes for a little while, then goes."
"How do I send it away?" Bami asked. Mom pointed to the frosted window. "Breathe on that ice. In through your nose, then a warm, slow breath out."

Bami breathed in, tummy rounding, then breathed onto the window. The frost melted in a circle, revealing snowy mountains! Their hot chest cooled, too. Mom sang, "Feeling angry? Breathe on the window!"
Bami looked at the shelf. "Pipi, sorry I shouted. I got angry all at once." Spreading their wings, Bami tapped the seat. "Sit with me. We have a clear circle now!"
Pipi fluttered down and nestled beside Bami. "It's okay!" Together they watched snowy mountains through the circle. Mom set warm tea on the table.
Pipi sipped Bami's tea. Anger stirred again. Bami quickly breathed in, then onto the window. "We can share. One, stop when angry! Two, breathe in! Three, breathe on the window!"
Mom nuzzled Bami's cheek. "Wonderful at sending anger away!" A breath, rather than a shout, helped anger leave. Feeling angry? Breathe on the window! Bami and Pipi laughed at their seat.
